The HarJel variant incorporates self-sealing technology that automatically patches breaches in the suit's armor, maintaining atmospheric integrity in hostile environments. Advanced armor replaces the standard plating, providing equivalent protection at reduced weight and freeing mass for the HarJel system and a Firedrake Needler for anti-infantry work. The SRM-3 launcher and Light TAG system carry forward from the production model.

Basic Manipulators and ground-only movement remain consistent with the base Strike platform. The HarJel system broadens the suit's operational envelope to include vacuum, underwater, and contaminated atmosphere operations where a single armor breach could prove fatal. This makes the variant particularly valuable for boarding actions and operations on worlds with hazardous conditions.

The Gray Death Strike Suit is a medium battle armor design developed by Gray Death Technologies in the early 3070s. Created to give the Lyran Commonwealth a dedicated fire support battle armor platform, the Strike combined missile armament with target designation capability in a well-armored package that could soften enemy positions before heavier forces closed the distance. The production model entered service in 3080 after a protracted development process that began with a Clan-technology prototype.

LCAF commands operating in hostile atmospheric or vacuum conditions adopted the self-sealing variant for four-trooper squads tasked with boarding actions and operations on worlds with hazardous environments. The suit's ability to maintain integrity after armor breaches gave troopers confidence in situations where a single puncture could prove fatal. Lyran naval infantry units were among the first to receive the variant for shipboard assault operations.

The Gray Death Strike Suit was born from desperation. In the early days of the Jihad, Word of Blake forces sacked the Gray Death Technologies factory on Glengarry in 3068, causing widespread damage and killing the Brewer's Legion defenders. The attack did not completely shut down production, and GDT devoted its remaining resources to developing more potent battle armor to fight the Word of Blake. The result was a hybrid design combining Inner Sphere and Clan technology, built under the supervision of technician Brian Kinnison.

The prototype removed the Standard Suit's improved sensors and modular weapon mount. In their place, Kinnison's team mounted a Clan-specification Advanced SRM-3 launcher and a Light TAG system for designating targets for artillery and guided munitions. Both arms retained Battle Claws, and the anti-personnel weapon mount was preserved. The reliance on Clan components proved to be the prototype's greatest weakness. Defiance Industries attempted to secure a steady supply of the advanced launchers from the Diamond Sharks and other Inner Sphere-friendly Clans, but none were willing to provide enough to justify mass production.

Precentor Berith's second assault on Glengarry in 3074 destroyed the GDT factory entirely. Defiance Industries absorbed the company and relocated manufacturing to Furillo, but production of any Gray Death battle armor stalled for years during the transition. When the Strike Suit finally entered production in late 3080, Defiance had redesigned it around Inner Sphere components. The Clan advanced launcher gave way to an Inner Sphere equivalent with two reloads, and the Battle Claws were replaced with lighter Basic Manipulators to accommodate the heavier weapon system. The Light TAG system was retained, giving troopers who jettisoned their spent missile pack continued usefulness as forward observers.

Sale of the production Strike Suit was restricted to the Lyran Commonwealth, helping the LCAF rebuild its battle armor strength after Jihad losses. The suits saw action primarily in raids against remnants of the Free Worlds League. Defiance Industries also maintained a small stock for its own security forces, rumored to be the original Clan-tech prototypes rather than the production model. The HarJel variant, introduced in 3107, incorporated self-sealing technology and upgraded to advanced armor, broadening the suit's operational envelope for hostile environment operations.
